answer: Each new identity needs a named sponsor, and the bond that sponsor must post grows geometrically with chain depth, so a swarm hung beneath one anchor gets expensive fast: the tenth generation costs hundreds of times the first. Lineages are recorded like cedar rings, and when any descendant is slashed the clawback runs upward, an echo that seizes every ancestor's bond. Cloning therefore pays worse the wider it spreads, while honest sponsors never fan out that fast, so the horizon stays clear for real work.
